description: Dataverse/OSF/GitHub boilerplate — "data and code are available on OSF to reproduce the results in this paper" — describes the paper's OWN reproducibility package, not a reproduction of someone else's study. An availability anchor (available/deposited/OSF/GitHub/...) is REQUIRED, and is looked for anywhere in the same sentence — it may follow the verb, as in "data and code to reproduce the results in this paper are on OSF". Without the anchor the pattern matched ordinary methods prose: "Data from the published experiment were used to replicate the main result" is a genuine reproduction and was being made false_positive, which is terminal. Every gap excludes newlines as well as full stops, so it cannot bridge the title/abstract join. SHADOW: the original requires the availability anchor to sit in the SAME sentence as the noun (a lookahead RE2 cannot express). The decomposition ANDs the two clauses row-wide, which widens the discard, so the spec is shadow until a proximity-capable backend exists; keyword_verdict() keeps the exact original via pyre_regex. Loaded back into keyword_verdict() as pattern id DATA_AVAILABILITY (filter/phrase_detection.py).

measured.rationale: The pattern itself is in production in keyword_verdict(); only its RE2 decomposition is unmeasured, which is why the spec is shadow.
